title: Two Sum
text: Given an integer array and a target, return the indices of the two elements that add up to the target. Exactly one valid pair exists.
hints: What must you have already seen to complete a pair at the current element?
Checking all pairs is O(n^2). What gives O(1) lookup?
Scan once, storing value->index; look up target-x before inserting x.
idea: One pass with a hash map from value to index: for each x check target-x, then record x.

title: Contains Duplicate
text: Decide whether any value appears at least twice in an array.
hints: Sorting is one way; what is another that needs no sort?
A set remembers what you have seen.
Return true as soon as an insert finds the value already present.
idea: Insert into a hash set while scanning; a repeated value means a duplicate.

title: Valid Anagram
text: Check whether one string is a rearrangement of another.
hints: What property of the two strings must match?
Count characters instead of sorting.
One counter: add for the first string, subtract for the second; all zeros means anagram.
idea: Compare character frequency tables (or sorted strings).

title: Group Anagrams
text: Group the words of a list so that words in a group are anagrams of each other.
hints: Two anagrams share something identical. What?
Turn each word into a canonical key.
Key = sorted letters or a 26-count tuple; map key -> list of words.
idea: Hash map from canonical form (sorted string or letter counts) to the group.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
text: Return the k values that occur most often in an array.
hints: First you need frequencies. Then what selects the top k?
A heap of size k or a bucket per frequency.
Bucket sort by frequency gives O(n).
idea: Count with a hash map, then take top k using a size-k min-heap or frequency buckets.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
text: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers that appear in an unsorted array, in linear time.
hints: Sorting is O(n log n). How could you avoid it?
Only start counting from numbers that begin a run.
A number x starts a run if x-1 is not in the set.
idea: Put values in a set; for each run start, walk upward counting; every element is visited once.

title: Product of Array Except Self
text: For each position, compute the product of all other elements, without using division.
hints: What do the elements to the left and right of i contribute?
Build a prefix product and a suffix product.
Reuse the output array to store prefixes, then multiply by a running suffix.
idea: Two passes: left-product prefix, then right-product suffix multiplied in.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
text: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k (values may be negative).
hints: Negative values break a sliding window. What replaces it?
Sum of a subarray = difference of two prefix sums.
Count earlier prefixes equal to current-k.
idea: Running prefix sum with a hash map of prefix-sum frequencies.

title: Valid Palindrome
text: Check whether a string reads the same both ways after ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and case.
hints: Where should the two pointers start?
Skip characters that do not count.
Compare in lower case and move inward.
idea: Two pointers from both ends, skipping non-alphanumerics.

title: 3Sum
text: Return all unique triples in an array that sum to zero.
hints: Reduce it to a problem you know: fix one number.
Sort first; then it is Two Sum on a sorted array.
Skip duplicates at all three positions.
idea: Sort, fix i, run two pointers on the rest, skip duplicate values.

title: Container With Most Water
text: Given bar heights, choose two bars that hold the most water between them.
hints: Area depends on width and the shorter bar.
Start with the widest pair.
Move the pointer at the shorter bar; moving the taller cannot help.
idea: Opposite-end pointers, always advancing the shorter side.

title: Trapping Rain Water
text: Given an elevation map, compute how much rain water is trapped.
hints: Water above a cell depends on the tallest walls on both sides.
Precompute left-max and right-max, or use two pointers.
Advance the pointer with the smaller max; its water level is determined.
idea: Two pointers with running left/right maxima, accumulating max - height.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
text: Given daily prices, find the maximum profit from one buy followed by one sell.
hints: For each day, what is the best day to have bought?
Track the minimum price so far.
Profit today = price - minSoFar.
idea: Scan once, tracking the minimum price and best difference.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
text: Find the length of the longest substring in which all characters are distinct.
hints: What makes a window invalid?
Shrink from the left until the duplicate is gone.
Store last-seen index to jump the left edge.
idea: Sliding window with a map of last positions; move left past the previous occurrence.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
text: With at most k character replacements, find the longest substring of one repeated letter.
hints: A window is valid if size - (most frequent count) <= k.
You do not need to shrink the max count exactly.
Keep a running max frequency; slide, do not shrink below best size.
idea: Window with frequency counts; grow right, move left when replacements needed exceed k.

title: Minimum Window Substring
text: Find the smallest substring of s that contains every character of t (with multiplicity).
hints: Track how many required characters are still missing.
Expand until valid, then shrink while still valid.
Maintain a 'formed' counter instead of comparing maps each step.
idea: Two pointers with need/have counts and a formed counter; record the best window when valid.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
text: Report the maximum of every window of size k as it moves across an array.
hints: A heap works but has stale entries. Is there something cheaper?
Keep candidates in decreasing order.
Store indices in a deque; drop the front when out of window, pop back while smaller.
idea: Monotonic decreasing deque of indices; the front is the window max.

title: Valid Parentheses
text: Check that brackets of three types in a string are correctly matched and nested.
hints: What is the most recent unmatched opener?
LIFO matching suggests which structure?
Push openers, pop on closer and compare; stack must be empty at the end.
idea: Stack of open brackets matched against each closer.

title: Daily Temperatures
text: For each day, find how many days until a warmer temperature.
hints: You want the next greater element to the right.
Keep unresolved days on a stack.
Pop while the current temperature is higher, recording the gap.
idea: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices; resolve popped days.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
text: Find the area of the largest rectangle under a histogram of bar heights.
hints: For each bar, how far can it extend left and right?
Next smaller element on each side.
Use a stack; when popping a bar, its width is between the new top and the current index.
idea: Monotonic increasing stack; compute area on each pop, with a sentinel at the end.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
text: Evaluate an arithmetic expression given in reverse Polish notation.
hints: Operands come before their operator.
What do you do when you see an operator?
Pop two, apply, push the result (mind operand order).
idea: Stack of operands; apply each operator to the top two.

title: Binary Search
text: Find a target in a sorted array or report that it is absent.
hints: What does each comparison let you discard?
Decide on inclusive or exclusive bounds and stay consistent.
Use mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 to avoid overflow.
idea: Classic binary search halving the range.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
text: Search for a value in a sorted array that has been rotated at an unknown pivot.
hints: At any mid, one half is sorted.
Check whether the target lies in the sorted half.
Decide which half is sorted by comparing nums[lo] and nums[mid].
idea: Modified binary search, discarding the half that cannot contain the target.

title: Koko Eating Bananas
text: Find the minimum eating speed that finishes all piles within h hours.
hints: If speed s works, does s+1 work?
That monotonicity allows searching over speeds.
Feasibility check sums ceil(pile / s).
idea: Binary search on the answer with a linear feasibility check.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
text: Find the smallest element of a rotated sorted array with distinct values.
hints: Compare mid with the right end.
If nums[mid] > nums[hi] the minimum is to the right.
Converge lo and hi without skipping the answer.
idea: Binary search comparing mid to hi to locate the rotation point.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
text: Find the median of two sorted arrays in logarithmic time.
hints: Think of partitioning both arrays so the left halves hold half of all elements.
Binary search the partition of the shorter array.
Valid when maxLeftA <= minRightB and maxLeftB <= minRightA.
idea: Binary search on the cut position in the smaller array, checking the partition invariants.

title: Reverse Linked List
text: Reverse a singly linked list.
hints: Which pointers must change for each node?
Keep prev, current and next.
Save next before overwriting current.next.
idea: Iteratively rewire next pointers (or recurse).

title: Linked List Cycle
text: Determine whether a linked list contains a cycle.
hints: A set of visited nodes works. Can you use O(1) space?
Two pointers moving at different speeds.
If they ever meet there is a cycle.
idea: Floyd's tortoise and hare.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
text: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
hints: Compare the two heads repeatedly.
A dummy head removes special cases.
Append the remainder when one list ends.
idea: Iterative merge with a dummy node and a tail pointer.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
text: Remove the n-th node counted from the end of a linked list in one pass.
hints: How do you know where the end is without knowing the length?
Keep two pointers n apart.
Use a dummy head in case the first node is removed.
idea: Advance the lead pointer n steps, then move both until the lead reaches the end.

title: LRU Cache
text: Design a cache with get and put in O(1) that evicts the least recently used entry at capacity.
hints: You need O(1) lookup and O(1) reordering.
Hash map plus doubly linked list.
Move a node to the front on every access; evict from the back.
idea: Hash map from key to node in a doubly linked list ordered by recency.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
text: Return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.
hints: What does a null node return?
Depth of a node = 1 + max of its children.
Iterative BFS by level also works.
idea: Recursive DFS returning 1 + max(left, right).

title: Invert Binary Tree
text: Mirror a binary tree by swapping left and right children everywhere.
hints: What is the operation at a single node?
Apply it recursively.
Base case: null.
idea: Swap children, recursing into both.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
text: Check whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree.
hints: Comparing only with the parent is not enough.
Pass down allowed (lo, hi) bounds.
In-order traversal must be strictly increasing.
idea: DFS with min/max bounds, or an in-order check.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
text: Find the lowest node that has both given nodes as descendants.
hints: What does a subtree report to its parent?
Return the node if it is one of the targets.
If both sides return non-null, the current node is the answer.
idea: Post-order DFS returning the target or the LCA found below.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
text: Return the node values level by level.
hints: What structure processes nodes in arrival order?
Snapshot the queue size at each level.
Loop exactly size times per level.
idea: BFS with a queue, collecting one list per level.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
text: Find the length of the longest path between any two nodes in a tree.
hints: The best path bends at some node.
Path through a node = left height + right height.
Update a global best while returning height.
idea: DFS returning height and tracking the max left+right.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
text: Find the maximum sum over any path in a binary tree (values may be negative).
hints: Distinguish the path you return upward from the best path bending here.
Ignore negative child contributions.
Upward gain = value + max(0, best child).
idea: DFS computing best downward gain while updating a global answer at every node.

title: Number of Islands
text: Count connected groups of land cells in a grid of land and water.
hints: Each land cell belongs to exactly one island.
Flood-fill from an unvisited land cell.
Mark visited by mutating the grid or a set.
idea: Scan the grid; on new land, DFS/BFS to mark the whole island and count it.

title: Clone Graph
text: Create a deep copy of a connected undirected graph.
hints: How do you avoid cloning a node twice?
Map original -> clone.
Create the clone before visiting neighbours to handle cycles.
idea: DFS/BFS with a map from original nodes to their clones.

title: Course Schedule
text: Given prerequisite pairs, decide whether all courses can be completed.
hints: Model courses as a directed graph. What makes it impossible?
A cycle.
Kahn's algorithm: process nodes of in-degree 0.
idea: Topological sort (Kahn) or DFS cycle detection with three states.

title: Rotting Oranges
text: Simulate rot spreading each minute across a grid and return the minutes until all fresh oranges rot, or -1.
hints: Several sources spread at the same time.
Start BFS from all rotten oranges together.
Count fresh oranges to detect the impossible case.
idea: Multi-source BFS by levels; each level is a minute.

title: Word Ladder
text: Find the shortest sequence of single-letter changes from one word to another using words from a list.
hints: Words are nodes; edges connect words differing by one letter.
Unweighted shortest path means BFS.
Generate neighbours through wildcard patterns like h*t.
idea: BFS over words, using pattern buckets to find neighbours quickly.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
text: Count the connected components given n nodes and an edge list.
hints: Each edge either merges two components or is redundant.
Union-Find tracks merges.
Start with n components and subtract one per successful union.
idea: Union-Find with path compression, decrementing the component count on each union.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
text: Return the k-th largest element of an unsorted array.
hints: Sorting works. Can you do better for small k?
Keep the k largest seen so far.
A min-heap of size k has the answer at its top.
idea: Size-k min-heap (or quickselect for average O(n)).

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
text: Merge k sorted linked lists into a single sorted list.
hints: At each step, which node is next?
The smallest among the k current heads.
Push (value, list index) into a heap.
idea: Min-heap of list heads; pop the smallest and push its successor.

title: Merge Intervals
text: Merge all overlapping intervals in a list.
hints: Order matters. What should you sort by?
After sorting by start, only the last merged interval can overlap.
Overlap when next.start <= last.end.
idea: Sort by start and sweep, extending or appending.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
text: Find the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap.
hints: Equivalent to keeping the maximum number of compatible intervals.
Sort by end time.
Keep an interval if it starts at or after the last kept end.
idea: Greedy by earliest end; count skipped intervals.

title: Jump Game
text: Each element is the max jump length from that position; decide if the last index is reachable.
hints: Track the furthest index reachable so far.
If the current index exceeds it, you are stuck.
Work backwards with a goal pointer as an alternative.
idea: Greedy scan maintaining the furthest reachable index.

title: Climbing Stairs
text: Count the distinct ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps at a time.
hints: How can you arrive at step n?
From n-1 or n-2.
Only the last two values are needed.
idea: Fibonacci-style DP: ways[n] = ways[n-1] + ways[n-2].

title: House Robber
text: Maximise the sum from a row of houses without picking two adjacent ones.
hints: At each house you either take it or skip it.
State: best up to i.
best[i] = max(best[i-1], best[i-2] + value[i]).
idea: 1D DP with two rolling variables.

title: Coin Change
text: Find the fewest coins needed to make an amount, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Greedy fails for some coin sets.
dp[a] = fewest coins for amount a.
dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]) over coins c.
idea: Bottom-up unbounded knapsack DP.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
text: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
hints: Define dp[i] as the best ending at i.
O(n^2) works; there is an O(n log n) improvement.
Maintain the smallest possible tail for each length and binary search it.
idea: DP O(n^2), or patience sorting with binary search on tails.

title: Unique Paths
text: Count paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of a grid moving only right or down.
hints: Each cell is reached from above or from the left.
Keep only one row.
idea: 2D DP over the grid (or the combinatorial formula).

title: Longest Common Subsequence
text: Find the length of the longest subsequence common to two strings.
hints: Compare the last characters of both prefixes.
Equal: 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise take the max of dropping one.
Rolling rows reduce memory.
idea: 2D DP table over prefixes of both strings.

title: Edit Distance
text: Compute the minimum insertions, deletions and replacements to turn one string into another.
hints: Base cases: converting to/from the empty string.
Three choices when characters differ.
dp[i][j] = 1 + min(insert, delete, replace).
idea: 2D DP table over prefixes.

title: Word Break
text: Decide whether a string can be split into words from a dictionary.
hints: Define dp[i] as: the first i characters can be segmented.
Try every split point j < i.
Use a set for the dictionary.
idea: 1D DP over prefixes with dictionary lookups.

title: Subsets
text: Return all subsets of a list of distinct integers.
hints: For each element you either include it or not.
Build the subset incrementally and record at every node.
Copy the current path when recording.
idea: Backtracking over include/exclude choices.

title: Permutations
text: Return all orderings of a list of distinct integers.
hints: Choose an unused element for each position.
Track used elements.
Swap in place as an alternative to a used array.
idea: Backtracking that fills positions with unused elements.

title: Combination Sum
text: Find all combinations of candidates (reusable) that sum to a target.
hints: Avoid duplicate orderings.
Only allow choosing candidates from index i onward.
Prune when the remaining sum is negative.
idea: Backtracking with a start index; the same element may be reused.

title: N-Queens
text: Place n queens on an n x n board so that none attack each other.
hints: Place one queen per row.
Track columns and both diagonals.
Diagonals: r-c and r+c are constant.
idea: Backtracking by row with column and diagonal sets.

title: Implement Trie
text: Implement a prefix tree supporting insert, search and startsWith.
hints: Each node maps characters to children.
Mark the end of a word explicitly.
startsWith just walks the prefix.
idea: Trie of nodes with a children map and an end flag.

title: Word Search
text: Check whether a word can be traced through adjacent cells of a grid without reusing a cell.
hints: Start a DFS from every matching first letter.
Mark a cell as visited while exploring, then unmark.
Prune as soon as a character mismatches.
idea: Grid DFS with backtracking on the visited state.
